gen_risks.description: A drop in agricultural output market prices exceeding 10 percent would cause net present values to turn negative and internal rates of return to fall below the cost of capital, undermining financial viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish aggregation centers, grain exchange platforms, and structured out-grower business alliances with off-takers to secure market prices and smooth seasonal volatility.
gen_risks.evidence: if benefits were reduced by 20 percent... the net present values will turn negative while the IRR were also below the cost of capital.

gen_risks.description: Low procurement capacity and lack of standardized procurement tools in participating states could cause procurement delays, inappropriate contract awards, and slow project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Competitive recruitment of experienced state procurement officers backed by an expert procurement consultant hired by the NCO to train and support state staff.
gen_risks.evidence: The procurement capacity is still considered low and most of the states do not have procurement tools in place.

gen_risks.description: Unretired travel advances and inadequate supporting documentation for expenditures in PFMUs and FPFMD could lead to ineligible expenses, financial mismanagement, and delayed disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce an enhanced accountability framework in the Financial Procedures Manual, including strict advance acquittal rules and risk-based internal auditing.
gen_risks.evidence: The key issues noted within the PFMUs and FPFMD are unretired advances and inadequate documentation of the eligible expenditures incurred.

gen_risks.description: Civil insecurity, regional unrest, or militant activities in project regions could threaten project personnel, disrupt supply chains, and delay physical infrastructure works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Concentrate interventions in secure agricultural clusters, maintain close security monitoring, and actively engage local community leadership and stakeholders.
gen_risks.evidence: compound by additional factors including a sharp drop in oil production levels due to militant activities in the Niger Delta region

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition for processing clusters and infrastructure could cause involuntary resettlement, loss of access to common resources like grazing lands, and community disputes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) to screen all civil works, minimize land acquisition, and implement site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) where required.
gen_risks.evidence: infrastructure investments could result in involuntary re-settlement and land requisition

gen_risks.description: Intensified use of agricultural chemicals (fertilizers, pesticides) and small civil works could pollute soil and surface water, generate runoffs, and damage local ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute environmental screening under the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and implement the Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP).
gen_risks.evidence: agricultural intensification involving the use of inputs, could potentially have adverse impact on soil, water and vegetation covers.

gen_risks.description: Extending power lines, gas pipelines, and utilities to processing clusters could encroach upon or degrade sensitive natural habitats such as swamps and marshes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict site screening under Operational Policy 4.04 (Natural Habitats) to route infrastructure lines away from ecologically sensitive wetlands.
gen_risks.evidence: extension of electricity transmission lines and installation of gas pipelines might pass through important natural habitats such as swamps and marshes.

gen_risks.description: Prevalence of fake or adulterated agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizer, agro-chemicals) on the market could depress crop productivity and cause financial loss to farmers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to FMARD and regulatory bodies (e.g., NASC, NAFDAC) to strengthen input quality control and accredit reliable agro-dealers.
gen_risks.evidence: support to FMARD... on quality control of agro-inputs such as seeds, fertilizer and agro-chemicals to address issues of adulteration

gen_risks.description: Delays by participating states in ratifying subsidiary agreements or issuing legal opinions could block disbursements under Categories 1, 2, and 3 and freeze state operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide early technical and legal support to state governments during project preparation to ensure rapid execution and legal ratification of subsidiary agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made... with respect to any Participating State unless the Association has received an opinion... that the Subsidiary Agreement has been duly authorized

gen_risks.description: Weak producer negotiation capacity, mistrust, or side-selling by farmers could lead to contract default in out-grower schemes and business alliances with commercial buyers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure formal business alliance contracts, build governance and managerial capacity in producer cooperatives, and engage dedicated business development service providers.
gen_risks.evidence: weak market negotiation ability of small producers vis-à-vis buyers and input providers to obtain better prices and more stable market relationships

gen_risks.description: Gender disparities in access to productive land, credit, and technology could exclude women farmers from full participation in value chain opportunities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Sub-component 2.1 startup grants dedicated to women and youth, setting a target of at least 50% female participation monitored via a gender tracker.
gen_risks.evidence: women in Nigeria, compared with men, have relatively limited access to productive agricultural land, inputs and services.

gen_risks.description: High commercial interest rates (up to 29 percent) and restricted credit availability could prevent farmers and agribusiness SMEs from securing complementary working capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide direct catalytic grant funding (matching and startup grants) and build commercial linkages between farmer cooperatives, off-takers, and financial institutions.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited access to financial services and high cost of capital is a serious constraint to modernization of the agriculture sector in Nigeria.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate management structures or lack of clear operation and maintenance (O&M) funding arrangements could lead to rapid deterioration of common processing facilities and link roads.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require established management structures and 100 percent beneficiary commitment to coverage of O&M costs prior to financing common infrastructure assets.
gen_risks.evidence: establish a management structure and O&M arrangement for each infrastructure before investing in such undertakings.

gen_risks.description: Disruptions or delays during the 18-month transition and competitive recruitment of permanent APPEALS project staff from the existing CADP structure could slow initial implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Retain experienced CADP core staff during the initial 18-month period while conducting competitive recruitment under World Bank oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: During the first 18-month period of project implementation, it is expected that selection and replacement of CADP staff will be completed

gen_risks.description: High post-harvest losses due to poor handling and lack of primary aggregation and cleaning facilities could reduce marketable volumes and lower income for producers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct and equip 90 commodity aggregation centers with post-harvest handling, sorting, cleaning, and cottage processing equipment.
gen_risks.evidence: support the reduction of post-harvest losses, facilitate the consolidation of produce and primary processing by farmers' cooperative societies

gen_risks.description: Erratic protectionist trade tariffs and border smuggling could destabilize domestic prices for key staples like rice and undercut domestic producer competitiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Improve domestic value chain efficiency and processing quality to build competitive advantages against smuggled goods, supported by policy dialogue with FMARD.
gen_risks.evidence: Erratic protectionist tariffs, which encourage smuggling of rice across borders

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic recession and oil revenue collapse could impair state government budgets, leading to liquidity shortages and fiscal stress across participating states.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide 100 percent IDA financing for project costs requiring no state counterpart funding, supported by performance-based resource allocations.
gen_risks.evidence: The collapse of oil prices and the liquidity crunch revived tensions between federal government and subnational governments regarding burden of the adjustment

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk has been rated Substantial. Coordination of externally funded projects' responsibilities between the federal and state levels is a complex phenomenon, and incomprehension or misinterpretation at any level can affect the project implementation negatively.
gt_risks.mitigation: A communication strategy, supported by the project, will ensure that transparency is maintained at all levels of project management and implementation, and the participation of beneficiaries remains at the core of the project.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risks are rated Substantial. Falling oil prices have undermined economic growth in the country and remain a major source of risks, which may be exacerbated further by security challenges, natural disasters, and climate change. With reliance on a few primary exports and a relatively undiversified economy, Nigeria remains vulnerable to external demand and price shocks, compounded by pressures from weak fiscal management.
gt_risks.mitigation: The World Bank is in close dialogue with the authorities on the reform program in support of restoring macro-economic resilience and economic growth.

gt_risks.description: Sector Policies and Strategies risk has been rated Substantial. One major risk is frequent changes in the agricultural policy, especially the tariff policy, which would change the economic incentives faced by farmers and the private sector alike. Considering this is a multi-sector project, risk associated with other sector policies (e.g., transport and energy) might also affect implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through a sustained, evidence-based policy dialogue and engagement with the government to ensure sustainability of the reforms in the sector.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design risk has been rated Moderate. The approach for agribusiness partnership proposed by this project has already been successfully implemented under CADP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Lessons learned from both CADP and other similar operations have been incorporated into the project design, which is based on analyses undertaken during preparation and summarized under Annex 2.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk has been rated Substantial. While capacity at the federal level for implementing World Bank-supported agricultural project activities is adequate, there is a risk at state level of insufficient experience, structure, and technical knowhow to manage the new project design features.
gt_risks.mitigation: SCOs' staff will be provided necessary training at the time of launching the project, and newly recruited staff (particularly in Kogi state) will benefit from an induction training program. Coordination challenges will be addressed by Steering Committees at federal and state levels, and a Technical Committee at state level chaired by the Commissioner of Agriculture. NCO and SCO will collaborate with FADAMAIII, RAMP, and GEM where relevant, and the project may contract a third-party service provider to assist states in project execution.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (financial management) is assessed as Substantial. The key risks identified are those of value for money in works/construction contracts and capacity building events; capacity building activities such as training workshops have been identified as having significant fiduciary risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: Additional steps include: (i) all training and workshop activities subject to prior review by the Bank; (ii) activities part of the approved annual work plan; (iii) part of the project training plan; and (iv) compliance with the enhanced accountability framework. A qualified procurement specialist will be selected competitively; goods and consultants' services will be procured in accordance with World Bank anti-fraud/corruption guidelines and procurement guidelines.

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk has been rated Substantial. The Environmental Category assigned to the project is Category B, predicated on the assumption that environmental risks and social impact may not have serious adverse impact of a sensitive or diverse nature; the project may not be engaged in development of heavy infrastructure or acquisition of large expanses of land.
gt_risks.mitigation: An Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) have been prepared and publicly disclosed. Specific Environment and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) will be conducted for each public and private investment once the type of work is determined and precisely located, and a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment will cover all areas and localities in which the project will operate.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholders/Gender risk: there is a risk that women will be disadvantaged in terms of their access to employment and participation in out-growers arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: A detailed gender assessment and tracking for the project will be undertaken with the DFID-supported Gender Filter Trust Fund, in collaboration with the Africa Gender Innovation Lab, and incorporated into the Project Implementation Manual. A substantial part of Component 2 (35% of project funding) will support a Women and Youth Empowerment program, with affirmation of 35 percent female inclusion in all aspects of the project (representation in joint community meetings, jobs, extension agents, facilitators, and agri-business/entrepreneurship development), plus TA and training on business plan preparation, accounting, and financial management for women.
